notes.title: Feature Release: 3D Physical Buttons
notes.notes:
Feature Release: 3D Physical Buttons

Just push them! This is exactly how buttons work in real life. No trigger necessary.

The trigger is no longer used in any UI element, so you'll never place a vertex by accident.

Here's a quick animated gif demo: http://i.imgur.com/k4CysCr.gifv

If pushing it doesn't work, try the grips. Some trigger actions have been moved to the grip buttons, like the snap spacing slider and the Object -> Open scroller.

Finally, the pointer cones now reflect the current fill color for a nice visual reminder.

notes.title: Feature Release: Save - Drive Letters, Documents, Downloads, and location
notes.notes:
Feature Release: Save - Drive Letters, Documents, Downloads, and location

Touchpad/Joystick changes:

Touchpad/Joystick -> Save now saves the last opened file, rather than blindly saving load.obj every time. This is a precursor to Save As, coming very soon.


The Object -> Open interface has the following changes:

 Drives - Any drives on your system should show up here ( C:\ for example ). What's more, the list will update in real time every two seconds, so feel free to plug that USB reader or stick.
 Special Folder shortcuts - We now have dedicated buttons for Documents, Downloads, and Desktop.
 Interface spawns like the other menus, tilted slightly away from the user for readability/comfort.
 New panel for drive letters and special folders is grabbable, so you can fine tune the positioning if desired.
 Panel grows to the right for long lists of drive letters or long paths. This is our first auto growing panel in MMVR. It's almost like we have the trappings of a basic UI now.

notes.title: Bug Fix Release: Handle materials with slightly different colors but same HTML name
notes.notes:
Bug Fix Release: Handle materials with slightly different colors but same HTML name

There was a bug in MMVR's automatic material naming code. Internally (and in the generated MTL file) we name materials based on the HTML color value. For example, if you edit a MTL file with a text editor, you'll see something like this:

[code]
newmtl Material_#E600FF00
Ka 1 1 1
Kd 0.9019608 0 1
Ks 0.5 0.5 0.5
Tf 1 1 1
Ke 0 0 0
Ns 96.07843
Ni 1
d 1
illum 2
[/code]

In the above example, "Material_#E600FF00" is the material name. "#E600FF00" is the HTML color value in this case. We were running into issues where materials with slightly different colors would have the same HTML color value. For example:

[code]
Kd 0.9019608 0 1
[/code]

and 

[code]
Kd 0.9019607 0 1
[/code]

both generate the same HTML color value #E600FF00.

In order to make MMVR more robust, this second color value will now generate a numerically ascending material name: "Material_#E600FF00_2"

We also fixed an issue with the alignment tool delete button a few days ago and rolled a release to fix the issue but didn't post an announcement. Consider this the announcement for that fix.

notes.title: Feature Release: Object -> Open interface for OBJ files
notes.notes:
Feature Release: Object -> Open interface for OBJ files

Tired of using load.obj in the application directory? Now you can use Tools -> Object -> Open to load a file from a folder of your choice. Careful! It doesn't ask you to save your work yet.

The interface is pretty bare bones right now, but it will improve with time. This is the first time I've seen a functional File -> Open dialog in VR. If it's not a first, it's rare, so there is a lot of UI Design frontier to explore.

Who wants to 3d design a recognizable folder mesh in Mesh Maker VR to replace our placeholder cubes?

notes.title: Feature Release: Preserve OBJ UVs and imports quads
notes.notes:
Feature Release: Preserve OBJ UVs and imports quads

New features:

 The OBJ loader in MMVR now preserves UVs (texture coordinates).
 The OBJ loader imports quad faces as two triangles now. You won't have to triangulate your quad meshes before loading in MMVR anymore.

Bug fixes:

 Reset wasn't resetting to 90 degree rotated position. This is fixed.
 Object scale followed Add/Move Vertex followed by Reset left vertices much too large. This is fixed.

notes.title: Bug Fix Release: Shader wasn't making it to production
notes.notes:
Bug Fix Release: Shader wasn't making it to production

MMVR has apparently been broken on Steam since April 10th. I didn't notice because it was working fine on all of my test machines. Only the production builds were broken. In other words, it was only broken for everyone but me. :(

This bug was caused by the new wireframe shader. I should have caught it, but I didn't. Sorry. My fault. I'll try to make sure I test the steam builds before they go out in the future.

It's fixed now. Big thanks to Chrisbot for reporting the issue last night and making me aware of it.

notes.title: Bug Fix Release: Performance Improvements
notes.notes:
Bug Fix Release: Performance Improvements

Performance Fixes:

 Sphere primitives were slowing down the framerate, especially using max vertices. There is still room for improvement, but this has been sped up and should be fairly quick now. Tested 100 FPS on an i7 with a GTX 970.
 Deletes should be much faster now.
 The wireframe subsystem has been completely overhauled. It is now a shader, which means 100% GPU. Big win for performance, but the triangle normals look pretty cool now too as they're thin little pyramids rather than simple lines.


Bug Fixes:

 Fixed bug where scaling an object down, adding a sphere, then switching to triangle select yielded oversized triangle selection outlines.

notes.title: Feature Release: Triangle Selection
notes.notes:
Feature Release: Triangle Selection

The recently added Fill tool has highlighted the need for a quick, easy way to select triangles.

This release renames the Selection section in the Tools Panel to Vertex Selection.

A new button has been added to the Vertex Selection section: "Select Verts by Triangles". Click this button, then click a triangle to select the surrounding vertices. Click the same triangle again to deselect the surrounding vertices, or click a different triangle to add to the selection.

A new section has also been added to the Tools Panel: Triangle Selection. This section has three buttons:

 Select Triangles - This differs from "Select Verts by Triangles" as it does not select the surrounding vertices, just the triangle itself. Vertices are hidden in this selection mode.
 Flip Normal - Select some triangles using Select Triangles, then click this button to flip the triangle normals.
 Fill - Select some triangles using Select Triangles, then click this button to color the triangles using the currently selected color in the Settings Panel.


The three multi select modes ("Select Vertices", "Select Verts by Triangles", and "Select Triangles") now allow clicking a previously selected item to deselect that item. Previously the only way to deselect an item was to clear the entire selection.

In addition, this release includes various bug fixes to primitives, extrusion, alignment tools, etc.

Happy VRing!

notes.title: Feature Release: Fill Tools
notes.notes:
Feature Release: Fill Tools

We now have the ability to color triangles/faces! This was a fairly massive undertaking and we're really excited about the potential of this awesome new feature.  

First, we needed a color picker tool. You'll find it in the Settings panel. Trigger click and drag the sliders to change colors. Your choice will be remembered across application restarts.

Next, we discovered the Wavefront OBJ library we were using didn't have MTL (material file) support, so we had to add that upstream. MMVR will now read and write the file "load.mtl" in the same folder as the file "load.obj". On our machines the path to these files is: "C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Mesh Maker VR"

This means you can save your work in MMVR and import it into Blender or any other application that reads Wavefront OBJ files with colors attached to faces. You can also go from Blender to MMVR just as easily with colors attached to faces.

Finally, we needed a way to fill triangles with the selected color. You'll find two "Fill" buttons in the Tools Panel. The first is in the Triangles section. This allows you to fill one triangle per click. The second button is in the Selection section and this allows you to fill multiple triangles at once from the current selection ( box select, etc ).

We also overhauled the selection visualization system and tweaked the lighting in MMVR so colors show up properly and are recognizable in various situations.

Extrusion has been improved to extrude, at first, along the average of the selected face normals now.

We have an eye dropper tool planned and we'd like to make colors visible in object mode as well as triangle modes. Stay tuned for more updates!

notes.title: Feature Release: Lock Reference Images
notes.notes:
Lock Reference Images

This is a checkbox in the Settings Panel now. When enabled, reference images may not be moved, resized, selected, etc. This allows the placement of vertices directly on the reference image without fear of placing an anchor by mistake. It also ensure the reference images do not move once they are in the correct positions.

Thanks to TrolliGan for bringing this problem to my attention through a bug report in the community forum.

Settings and Tool Panel location bug fix

A few releases ago I changed the way the Settings and Tool Panels pop into existence in relation to the user. I discovered a bug in this code this evening causing the panels to appear behind the controller pointer rather than in front of it, depending on the user's orientation in space. This should be fixed now.

Feature Release: Cylinder Primitives

To make a cylinder primitive, open the tools panel and click the Cylinder button under Primitives.

This feature behaves the same as Circle Primitives, but the second trigger click automatically extrudes the first circle, then flips it's normals. This is the first end cap. The third trigger click places the second end cap and selects the entire cylinder.

Use with snaps enabled for parallel end caps and exact placement.

Updated SteamVR Plugin

Updated SteamVR Plugin to version 1.2.1.

notes.title: Feature Release: Circle Primitives!
notes.notes:
Feature Release: Circle Primitives!

To make a circle primitive, open the tools panel and click the Circle button under Primitives. The first trigger click sets the center point. The second trigger click sets the radius, orientation, and number of vertices.

To set the orientation and radius, after the first trigger click but before the second, simply rotate and move the controller in space.

To set the number of vertices, after the first trigger click but before the second, tilt the controller toward or away from the circle. When the controller is in the same plane as the circle you will have the minimum number of vertices, which is five. Yes, I know, that's a pentagon, not a circle, but this is 3d modelling in VR, not real life, so you get a pentagon and you'll like it!

notes.title: Surprise Feature Release: 3d Scanner Mode
notes.notes:
Surprise Feature Release: 3d Scanner Mode

Enable from the Settings Panel. Flips pointer cone from top of the controller to the bottom so the controller can be used to "trace" real world objects, placing vertices around the perimeter of the object.

This feature wasn't planned. It was inspired by a suggestion from Routb3d on reddit. It was such a cool idea I had to give it a try.

Works with the Oculus Touch and HTC Vive, but the Vive is a little more reliable if the controller needs to be behind the object being scanned.

New grid floor texture

Thanks for the submission, Jacob!
Let us know if you prefer this texture to the old "moldy" bricks texture.

notes.title: Bug Fixes for vertex size after scaling and more
notes.notes:
Bug Fixes for vertex size after scaling and more

Vertex size after scaling
Scaling an object up or down changed the vertex size. This was the result of the performance optimizations we implemented as a result of box select. Fixed now.

Alignment tool placement incorrect when object rotated
Rotating an object then placing an alignment tool would result in incorrect orientation of alignment tool. This seems to have been a problem since alignment tools were implemented. Not sure why we didn't notice it earlier, but it's fixed now.

Scaling twice required reselection
Scaling once, then releasing one or both controllers and scaling again required moving the controllers away from the object (deselect) and back into the object (reselect). Fixed so object can be immediately rescaled without reselect.

Known issue: Object still appears unselected after first scale operation, but this is a visual bug only.

notes.title: New Feature Release: Pinch Scaling in Object mode
notes.notes:
New Feature Release: Pinch Scaling in Object mode

To pinch scale an object, it works pretty much as you'd expect:
[olist]
 Create or load an object with at least one Triangle or face
 Trigger click the Move Scale button under Objects in the Tools Panel
 Reach out and grip the object with one hand as if moving it. Don't let go.
 Reach out and grip the object with your other hand in a different spot.
 Move your hands apart to scale up, move your hands together to scale down.
 The object can still be rotated while scaling by rotating the hand you first gripped it with.
 Release either hand grip to exit scaling mode.
 To return to the initial scale, trigger click the Reset button under Objects in the Tools Panel.
[/olist]

This feature hasn't been through QA. Let us know if you find a bug.

Known Issues: The Settings Panel snap spacing scale doesn't resize after object has been scaled.
